steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Recent advances in VR/AR technologies show that there is a growing need to create immersive virtual environments. Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) is a technique that has gotten a lot of attention because it can generate photorealistic 3D scenes, which meets this demand for more immersion and realism. Using NeRF to create lifelike simulations is very valuable, especially for developing intelligent agents that can carry out real-world tasks. But dynamic NeRF is still a complex problem. Traditional NeRF deals with static scenes, while dynamic NeRF tries to capture and represent objects and scenes that change over time. So it needs to model complex temporal dynamics, like object motion, deformation, or interactions, and these can be hard to represent accurately. At the same time, it is also an interesting avenue to explore whether multimodal sensory data can make NeRF training better. This work focuses on egocentric view synthesis, which is a natural scenario with rich multimodal data that can be captured by multi-sensory wearable devices.

Progress in egocentric vision depends a lot on hardware advancements. This is especially relevant for wearable devices like Aria Glasses, which capture data from a first-person perspective in real-life scenarios. Aria Glasses were designed as a research tool to speed up advances in AR/VR, embodied AI, and human behavior modeling. They use a range of sensors to capture first-person video, audio, eye movement data and location, which gives a comprehensive platform for understanding what a user intends and how they interact with the world.

- Aria-NeRF Dataset
  - comprehensive multimodal egocentric dataset for multimodal egocentric scene modeling
  - diverse real-world multi-sensory data from Aria Glasses
  - rich testbed for NeRF tasks and algorithms; high-quality annotations
  - scalable; cost-effective pipeline from Aria videos to NeRF-compatible training data
- Contributions
  - task: Multimodal Egocentric Scene Modeling, Fisheye RGB images + multimodal sensory data
  - dataset modalities: Fisheye images, RGB, depth, IMU, audio, etc.; audio-guided, gaze-guided NeRF; language annotations for LLMs-guided NeRF
  - benchmark Nerfacto and NeuralDiff; dataset challenging, current NeRF methods need improvement

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Recent advances in VR/AR technologies show that there is a growing need to create immersive virtual environments. Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) is a technique that has gotten a lot of attention because it can generate photorealistic 3D scenes, which meets this demand for more immersion and realism. Using NeRF to create lifelike simulations is very valuable, especially for developing intelligent agents that can carry out real-world tasks. But dynamic NeRF is still a complex problem. Traditional NeRF deals with static scenes, while dynamic NeRF tries to capture and represent objects and scenes that change over time. So it needs to model complex temporal dynamics, like object motion, deformation, or interactions, and these can be hard to represent accurately. At the same time, it is also an interesting avenue to explore whether multimodal sensory data can make NeRF training better. This work focuses on egocentric view synthesis, which is a natural scenario with rich multimodal data that can be captured by multi-sensory wearable devices.

Progress in egocentric vision depends a lot on hardware advancements. This is especially relevant for wearable devices like Aria Glasses, which capture data from a first-person perspective in real-life scenarios. Aria Glasses were designed as a research tool to speed up advances in AR/VR, embodied AI, and human behavior modeling. They use a range of sensors to capture first-person video, audio, eye movement data and location, which gives a comprehensive platform for understanding what a user intends and how they interact with the world.

In this paper, we present the Aria-NeRF Dataset. It is a comprehensive multimodal egocentric dataset designed for multimodal egocentric scene modeling, and it has diverse real-world multi-sensory data captured with Aria Glasses. Extensive experiments show that our dataset is a rich testbed for typical NeRF-based tasks and algorithms, and it has high-quality annotations that future research can explore. Our dataset is also scalable, and it offers a cost-effective pipeline to convert videos captured with Aria Glasses into training data that is compatible with NeRF.

In summary, our main contributions are as follows:

- • We introduce the task of Multimodal Egocentric Scene Modeling, which is a step towards egocentric view synthesis with neural scene representations, using Fisheye RGB images and multimodal sensory data.

- • We build a novel Aria-NeRF Dataset with multiple modalities, such as Fisheye images, RGB, depth, IMU, audio, etc. The Aria-NeRF Dataset is a rich testbed for advancing multimodal NeRF, for example audio-guided NeRF and gaze-guided NeRF. In particular, the Aria-NeRF Dataset has language annotations, so it is suitable for training LLMs-guided NeRF.

- • We evaluate and benchmark Nerfacto and NeuralDiff on the Aria-NeRF Dataset extensively. The results show that our dataset and egocentric view synthesis are challenging, which suggests that current NeRF methods need further improvement.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Recent advances in VR/AR technologies highlight a growing need for creating immersive virtual environments. Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) [1] is a technique that has gained much attention for its capability to generate photorealistic 3D scenes, meeting this demand for greater immersion and realism. Using NeRF to create lifelike simulations is of significant value, particularly for developing intelligent agents capable of executing real-world tasks. Nevertheless, dynamic NeRF remains a complex problem [2]. Unlike traditional NeRF, which deals with static scenes, dynamic NeRF aims to capture and represent objects and scenes that change over time. This requires modeling complex temporal dynamics, such as object motion, deformation, or interactions, which can be challenging to represent accurately. On the other hand, it also opens an intriguing avenue to explore whether multimodal sensory data can enhance NeRF training. This work focuses on egocentric view synthesis, a natural scenario featuring rich multimodal data that can be captured by multi-sensory wearable devices.

The progress of egocentric vision [3,4] relies heavily on hardware advancements. This is particularly relevant for wearable devices like Aria Glasses [5,6], which capture data from a first-person perspective in real-life scenarios. Aria Glasses, designed as a research tool to accelerate advances in AR/VR, embodied AI, and human behavior modeling, employ a range of sensors to capture first-person video, audio, eye movement data and location, providing a comprehensive platform for understanding a user's intention and their interactions with the world.

In this paper, we present the Aria-NeRF Dataset, a comprehensive multimodal egocentric dataset designed for multimodal egocentric scene modeling, with diverse real-world multi-sensory data captured using Aria Glasses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our dataset is a rich testbed for typical NeRF-based tasks and algorithms, with high-quality annotations for future research to explore. Our dataset is also scalable, offering a cost-effective pipeline for converting videos captured with Aria Glasses into NeRF-compatible training data.

In summary, our main contributions are as follows:

- • We introduce the task of Multimodal Egocentric Scene Modeling, a step towards egocentric view synthesis with neural scene representations, using Fisheye RGB images and multimodal sensory data.

- • We build a novel Aria-NeRF Dataset, which includes multiple modalities, such as Fisheye images, RGB, depth, IMU, audio, etc. The Aria-NeRF Dataset serves as a rich testbed for advancing multimodal NeRF, for example audio-guided NeRF and gaze-guided NeRF. In particular, the Aria-NeRF Dataset has language annotations, which make it suitable for training LLMs-guided NeRF.

- • We evaluate and benchmark Nerfacto [7] and NeuralDiff [8] extensively on the proposed Aria-NeRF Dataset. The results reveal the challenging nature of our dataset and of egocentric view synthesis, suggesting that current NeRF methods need further improvement.
